items.source_name: Daily Jagran (live blog) / BBC News India / India Today / Inshorts / Kashmir In Focus
items.summary: Escalation from the earlier police visit (~2:10 PM IST): Delhi Police served CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke a written notice at NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande's residence, where he is staying. The notice states Section 163 BNSS is in effect in Connaught Place and that NDMC gave no permission for the 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march — a breach would be a Section 163 violation inviting legal action. Inshorts reports the notice bars him from holding the Tiranga march in Connaught Place this evening. Dipke signed/received the document (India Today: exact terms unconfirmed) and released a video statement, carried by BBC News India, saying 7–8 officers accused him of 'unlawful activities and inciting people' and told him he 'cannot go wave the tricolour,' expressing dismay at being prevented from raising the national flag in his own country. No detention has been confirmed; the 5 PM march remains called.
items.title: Delhi Police serves Abhijeet Dipke a written notice barring the Tiranga march; Dipke records video response
